docs.title: WUWEI 无为
docs.text:
Responsible autonomy for agent teams. Your agents plan, build, review and ship. WUWEI audits the evidence, holds the few doors that do not reopen, and asks you only what is yours.

无为 (wuwei, said woo-way) means "effortless action": work gets done without forcing it.

docs.title: The problem it solves
docs.text:
Agents are fast, tireless and literal. They take the shortest path to "done": a merge without the test, a review skipped, a force push to make a conflict go away. They also ask too much: should I continue, which name do you prefer, may I run the tests. Both cost you. The first costs quality, the second costs your attention.

Adding process usually makes it worse. A process the model cannot see the point of is a process it routes around, and every rule you add to catch a workaround creates the next one.

docs.title: The idea
docs.text:
WUWEI does not prescribe steps. It describes what done looks like, reads the artifacts the work leaves behind (commits, pull requests, verdicts, CI), and says what is missing. The model chooses how to get there with its own tools.

Around that it adds three things:

  • Teaching at the moment. Hooks bring the right standard when it matters: the PR template before a PR opens, the verdict format when a review comes back malformed.
  • A few doors. A short, closed list of refusals for what cannot be taken back. Everything else passes and is recorded.
  • A learning loop. Each checkpoint's retro turns what escaped into standards, retires rules that never catch anything, and proposes memory and skills for your repositories.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Getting started: install and run your first day.
  • Concepts: every idea in WUWEI, why it is there, and where it lives.
  • Reference: commands, configuration, files and formats.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Claude Code, Python 3.11 or newer, Git and the GitHub CLI (gh), authenticated. WUWEI installs no packages: its runtime is the Python standard library.

WUWEI supports macOS, Linux and Windows with Python 3.11 or newer; CI runs the full test suite on all three with Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13. Its hooks look for Python 3.11 or newer in this order: WUWEI_PYTHON, then python3.15 down to python3.11, python3, py -3 (the Windows launcher) and python. The first one at 3.11 or later runs WUWEI. A harness can give hooks a shorter PATH than your shell, so an older python3 may come first there, for example macOS's /usr/bin/python3 3.9. When no interpreter fits, every tool call is refused with one line that names each interpreter tried and its version. Set WUWEI_PYTHON to the full path of a 3.11 or later interpreter to choose one. wuwei doctor names the interpreter it runs under and the one the hooks last used.

On Windows, Claude Code runs hooks through Git Bash, so install Git for Windows and Python from python.org (it brings py).

The doors read every command as bash. A command run through PowerShell, cmd, wsl or zsh (powershell -Command ..., cmd /c ...) is not unwrapped yet, so Codex on Windows, which runs PowerShell, and zsh on macOS get weaker doors than bash; a follow-up closes this.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
In Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add taoq-ai/wuwei
/plugin install wuwei@wuwei

For a verified install, use the signed wuwei.tar.gz release asset: it carries MANIFEST.sha256 and its signature.

docs.title: Create the workspace
docs.text:
The wuwei CLI is not on your PATH; it lives inside the installed plugin. From the directory that will own the workspace (usually your main repository), call it by its full path:

WUWEI=$(find ~/.claude/plugins -type f -path '*/bin/wuwei' | sort | tail -n 1)
"$WUWEI" init
"$WUWEI" doctor

Once the workspace exists, each session's start prints the path as WUWEI CLI: <path>, so the agents call it without help.

init creates .wuwei/ and merges WUWEI's rules into .claude/settings.json: an allow list for everyday work, deny rules for the doors, ask rules for infrastructure. Your own rules stay as they are. doctor checks the install and prints, per repository, how strongly each door holds.

Add more repositories by saying so, or with bin/wuwei config repos owner/a,owner/b.

On Codex, install with codex plugin marketplace add taoq-ai/wuwei and codex plugin add wuwei@wuwei, then run bin/wuwei init --codex; see running on Codex.

To run WUWEI in Claude Code on the web too, add --cloud and commit .claude/; see cloud sessions.

docs.title: Your first day
docs.text:
1. Open Claude Code in the workspace directory. The session starts oriented: the way of working, the decision and done rules, the board, and where the planner charter and your goals are.
  2. Run /wuwei-run. With no goals yet, it proposes up to three and asks you once. Then the lead ranks candidates, you see the plan as a view (.wuwei/plan.html), approve or change it, and the work starts.
  3. Work with the session as usual. You will be asked only one-way, scope, goal, trust, infrastructure, owner-review and exception questions.
  4. Run /wuwei-close when you stop. You get the report and the retro; planning again later reopens the day.

docs.title: Recommended: give the agents their own identity
docs.text: The strongest doors live on the code host, not on your machine. Give the agents a GitHub App or a machine user with write access and no admin rights, protect your default branches with a ruleset, and keep infrastructure credentials out of the agents' environment. Then a merge without review is impossible, not only refused. See the doors.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command What it does wuwei init [dir] [--cloud] Create .wuwei/ and merge WUWEI's allow, deny and ask rules into .claude/settings.json; --cloud also copies the plugin into .claude/ for cloud sessions; --codex writes the role agents and door rules into .codex/ wuwei sent owner/repo#n <link> Record a review request posted outside the session wuwei sync Pull, then push .wuwei/ on the wuwei/state branch wuwei doctor Install, workspace, ledger, harness rules, and each door's strength per repository wuwei plan [show] [<id>] The ranked plan; --json for machines; with an id, that item as JSON (promise and acceptance included) wuwei plan add <id> "<title>" --goal G-n --repo owner/name --tier smart\|light\|standard\|full Add an item (tier smart by default, with --domain "clear\|complicated\|complex: <one line of evidence>" and --in-doubt when the promise itself may be wrong) with --value --time --risk --size (WSJF) or --reach --impact --confidence --effort (RICE) and --why, --promise, one --accept per scenario, --class expedite\|fixed-date\|standard\|intangible (the class of service; at most one open expedite item), one --after <id> per item it waits on (never one that waits on it), --host agent\|session (where its builder runs: an Agent-tool seat, the default, or its own session; gates always run as Agent-tool seats in the planner's session; any other value is refused), and --pr owner/repo#n to link a PR whose body has no WUWEI footer (a taken-over PR; the board otherwise says PR owner/repo#n not linked); an id already in the plan is updated in place, and a changed promise or acceptance clears its approval wuwei plan add --from <file> Add the lead's candidates (.wuwei/candidates.json): a list, or {"candidates": [...]}, each with an id and a title; any other shape is refused and nothing is added wuwei plan restore <id> Reopen a parked or dropped item wuwei plan park\|drop\|done <id> --reason "..." Change an item's status wuwei plan run <id> --reason "<what ran, what it showed>" Record run evidence for an operations item; refused without --reason or --job wuwei plan run <id> --job <job file> Register a Codex companion job file; the board shows its state (running, completed with the HANDOFF path, failed, asked a question, or job state unreadable) wuwei plan session <id> <session id> Record the builder session of an open --host session item; while the item is open the board counts it as a live builder seat and names the session, and with no PR and no event for four hours shows the row stale; refused for an item with host agent or a done, parked or dropped item wuwei plan pass --reason "..." Record a plan pass; reopens a closed day wuwei plan view [--html] The plan as a view: writes .wuwei/plan.html, prints a summary and the question line (--html prints the page) wuwei status [--json] The board: what each open item lacks; past the WIP limit, an approved item with no PR shows queued wuwei evidence owner/repo#n [--json] [--record DIR] One PR's gaps; exit 1 when there are gaps wuwei report [--day YYYY-MM-DD] The day report wuwei report --dora [--window 28] The DORA keys per repository wuwei close Checkpoint: write the report for the day so far wuwei andon owner/repo --reason "..." / --clear Pull or clear the cord on one repository wuwei owe <thread link> "<what>" --who <name> [--within 4h \| --due <ISO>] Record a reply someone is waiting for wuwei watch [--record "<summary>"] The last watch pass and replies owed; record a pass wuwei status --all The board with process fit too (for the watch) wuwei config [key value] Show, or set one of the six keys wuwei verify Check the ledger's hash chain wuwei agents [check\|build] Check or build the role agents from the charters wuwei --version The plugin version wuwei hook <event> Called by the harness only

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
.wuwei/config.toml has six keys. Everything else is discovered or part of the process.

Key Default Meaning repos the origin of the init directory the repositories in the workspace owner_paths [] glob patterns you review yourself prioritisation wsjf wsjf or rice tracker github where issues live telemetry true local tool-call traces models {} your rows over the model table: "<role>[ <tier>]" = "<model> <effort>"; set with wuwei config models "builder light=opus medium"

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Path Holds .wuwei/plan.json the running queue .wuwei/goals.md the goals, the direction .wuwei/plan.html the plan view you approve .wuwei/standards.md rules the retro promoted, per role; a Review requests: <where> line names where reviews are asked; a Generated (<owner/repo>, <date>): <globs> line names files, off risky, owner and contract paths, whose change after a pass needs no delta review .wuwei/verdicts/<item>/ the sentinels' verdict files .wuwei/ledger/<clone>.jsonl the hash-chained record, one file per clone .wuwei/.gitignore keeps the state out of working branches; it travels on wuwei/state .wuwei/traces.jsonl local telemetry .wuwei/days/<date>/report.md each checkpoint's report .wuwei/retro/<date>.md the steward's retro .wuwei/canary the workspace canary token

docs.title: PR body lines
docs.text: Line When <sub>[WUWEI <version>](https://taoq-ai.github.io/wuwei/) · Item `<id>` · <title> · Goal <G-n> · Tier <tier></sub> always, last line; the older WUWEI-Item: <id> still links, with a process-fit line naming the footer No test: <reason> a change no test can hold Size: <reason> over about 400 changed lines Rollback: <how to undo> full tier, or owner_paths touched BREAKING CHANGE: <what> (and ! in the title) a major only: an incompatible change to the public API, as Breaking changes declares it; a stricter check of a rule the docs already state is a fix: (a patch) with release notes in the body Announcement: <url> a breaking change: one http(s) URL alone on the line, without brackets, of a communication that already exists (a PR or issue comment, or a published release note or migration guide); a changelog entry written at release does not count

docs.title: Verdict format
docs.text:
Verdict: PASS | FIX | ESCALATE
Gate: arch | quality | security | goal
Item: <plan item id>
PR: <owner/repo>#<number>   (or <owner/repo> alone before its draft PR exists)
Head: <the 40-character sha you reviewed>
Confidence: low | medium | high
Breaking: no | yes: <what breaks for which clients>   (arch only)

## Findings
- [critical|high|medium|low] <file>:<line> blocks: yes. Failure: <the concrete scenario>
- [low] <file>:<line> blocks: no. <a note>   (the <file>:<line> is optional on a note)
(or none)

A blocking finding names its <file>:<line>; a note without a place in the code leaves it out. The reviewer ends its report with Verdict file: <path>. A written verdict file is never edited: a corrected or second verdict for the same head goes to the next free <gate>-<sha7>-2.md.

docs.text:

useless rules go steward, .wuwei/standards.md Error budget Autonomy is earned by results and lost by escapes evidence tiers Calibration and gate yield Know which reviews pay and which reviewers are overconfident the report Skills and memory proposals Stop re-learning the same repository facts retro proposals Report, telemetry, DORA See what happened without asking wuwei report The ledger A tamper-evident record of what was decided .wuwei/ledger/ Replay cases The auditor itself is held to its past answers tests/replay/ Many repositories One process, the shape of each repository one workspace Running on Codex One process whichever agent does the work wuwei init --codex, .codex/ Cloud sessions A fresh clone starts where the last session stopped wuwei init --cloud, wuwei sync, the wuwei/state branch Work in progress Nothing waits on your nudge: PRs and replies keep moving /wuwei-watch, wuwei owe Finish before starting Too much open at once and nothing closes the WIP limit and seat ceiling, /wuwei-close housekeeping

docs.title: Cloud sessions
docs.text: WUWEI runs in Claude Code on the web the same way it runs on your machine, with two differences a cloud session forces: a repository's own plugins do not load there, and every session starts from a fresh clone, so nothing it does not put in git survives.

docs.title: Setting it up
docs.text:
In the repository the cloud sessions open, run once:

bin/wuwei init --cloud

and commit .claude/ to the default branch. It copies the plugin there: the CLI and the charters in .claude/wuwei/, the skills in .claude/skills/, the agents in .claude/agents/, and the five hooks in .claude/settings.json, pointing at the copy. Run it again after upgrading the plugin to refresh the copy.

The copy acts only in cloud sessions. On your machine the installed plugin serves, and the copy stays quiet, so the hooks never run twice.

Cloud sessions run a repository's hooks only when the session holds that one repository. In a session with two or more, no WUWEI hook fires: the doors are off, owner answers and gate verdicts are not recorded, and wuwei doctor warns hooks: no hook has fired here. Open a session that holds only the repository with .claude/wuwei/.

Code-host reads are REST, because cloud sessions refuse GraphQL. Review threads come from the session's own review-thread route when GraphQL is refused.

docs.title: State that survives the session
docs.text:
.wuwei/ travels on its own branch, wuwei/state, never in a working branch (its .gitignore ignores everything, so a PR never carries it by accident).

  • At a cloud session's start, the SessionStart hook pulls the branch, and rebuilds .wuwei/ when the clone has none.
  • When a cloud session stops, the Stop hook pushes what changed.
  • Anywhere, wuwei sync pulls then pushes; /wuwei-close runs it.

Each clone appends only to its own ledger file, .wuwei/ledger/<clone>.jsonl, with its own hash chain, and pushes only that file. Two sessions working at once never drop each other's records. The plan merges by item: each plan change stamps the items it changed, and for each item the newest stamp wins, so two clones that each add an item both keep both. Other files follow the last writer; a file changed both here and on the branch keeps the local copy and says so. Telemetry traces, caches and the canary stay on the machine.

Why: a fresh clone that forgot the plan, the rulings and the attestations would ask you again for everything you already decided. Keeping state beside the code, on a branch no PR touches, lets every session start where the last one stopped.

docs.title: Running on Codex
docs.text: WUWEI runs on OpenAI Codex from the same repository, with the same CLI, hooks, charters, skills and evidence. Codex reads Claude-style plugins (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, skills/, hooks/hooks.json) and runs Claude-style lifecycle hooks with the same events and output shapes, so there is no second plugin to keep in step.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
codex plugin marketplace add taoq-ai/wuwei
codex plugin add wuwei@wuwei

Then, in the directory that owns the workspace:

bin/wuwei init --codex

That writes what a Codex plugin cannot carry:

  • the eight role agents as .codex/agents/<role>.toml, with the charters as their instructions;
  • WUWEI's doors as exec-policy rules in .codex/rules/wuwei.rules (force pushes, admin merges and repository deletion forbidden; infrastructure applies and destroys prompted).

Codex asks you to trust a new or changed hook before it runs: trust WUWEI's five hooks once, and again after an upgrade changes them. Codex runs hooks through your login shell ($SHELL -lc) on macOS and Linux, and through cmd.exe on Windows, where it reads each hook's commandWindows entry: bin/wuwei.cmd. That entry tries WUWEI_PYTHON, then py -3, then python, and needs Python 3.11 or newer, as bin/wuwei does. The login shell may put an older python3 first, so if every call is refused with "WUWEI needs Python 3.11 or later", set WUWEI_PYTHON to a 3.11 or later interpreter where Codex starts, or install one as python3.12 or python3.13. Run wuwei init --codex again after an upgrade too; wuwei doctor warns while the role files differ from the charters.

docs.title: What maps to what
docs.text:
Claude Code Codex How WUWEI reads it Bash Bash (shell and exec) the same command guards Write, Edit apply_patch the files the patch adds, updates, deletes or moves to; the ledger stays protected Agent with subagent_type spawn_agent with agent_type a running seat; the Stop hook stays quiet while it runs AskUserQuestion request_user_input the same owner classes; answers recorded as answer.unconfirmed until WUWEI reads Codex's transcript mcp__server__tool mcp__server__tool the same leak and merge doors SubagentStop SubagentStop recorded as seat.unconfirmed, with no attestation, until WUWEI reads Codex's transcript .claude/settings.json rules .codex/rules/*.rules written by wuwei init and wuwei init --codex

On Claude Code each seat's model and effort come from the model table. On Codex the role files name no model: Codex chooses its own, and a Claude model name would not resolve there. The models page maps each step of the table to a Codex model. That column is the planner's reading of the Codex catalog, not OpenAI guidance on seats. It is unmeasured, and writing it into the role files is later work.

docs.title: Gates on Codex
docs.text:
A gate counts only when WUWEI attests its verdict from the seat's own hand-back or SubagentStop. Gates never go to Codex: a gate run as a codex-companion task or a Codex seat never counts. A codex-companion task job started from a Claude session is not a seat: it has no SubagentStop, so its verdict file sits unattested and wuwei evidence names it as not counted (#1078, #1181). Its job id does not change that: a job id is not a hand-back the harness recorded. A Codex-native seat (spawn_agent with agent_type sentinel-<gate>) goes through the same hooks, but its stop is recorded as seat.unconfirmed (#1172), so a Codex seat never counts either. Run gates as Claude seats; builders and fix rounds may run on Codex.

A brief for a seat on Codex tells it not to use MCP tools. Codex can deny an MCP call without asking, and a seat treats any denied call as a blocker, so one denial can stop a sound review.

Breaking change (hook-transcript, #1172): before it, a Codex request_user_input answer was recorded as a ruling by its question and a Codex seat's stop was attested. Now both are recorded as answer.unconfirmed and seat.unconfirmed, because WUWEI cannot yet read Codex's transcript to confirm them. Ask owner questions (owner review:, breaking:, exception:, plan:, goal:) and run gates from a Claude Code session, or approve on the code host. The rows name why, so nothing is lost silently.

Why: the process is the product, not the harness. The same evidence, doors and questions hold whichever agent does the work, and a team can run both without two rule books.

docs.title: Reversibility and confidence
docs.text:
Every open choice is weighed on two questions: can it be undone cheaply, and how sure are you?

Sure Unsure Undone cheaply act act, and record the assumption Hard to undo act, with a Rollback: line ask the owner

Why: most mistakes are cheap if they can be undone, so the model should act and keep moving. The expensive mistakes are the ones that are both hard to undo and uncertain, and those are the only ones worth your attention. This is the one-way and two-way door idea, made into a rule the model applies itself.

docs.title: Assumptions
docs.text:
A choice taken without asking is recorded under Assumptions: in the spec or PR body: what was assumed, why, and what would overturn it. Gates review assumptions like any other finding, and the steward samples them for reversals.

Why: an assumption written down can be checked and corrected. An assumption left in the model's head cannot.

docs.title: Asking the owner
docs.text:
A question reaches you only when it starts with its class:

Class For one-way: hard to undo and unsure scope: work outside the goals, a reviewer's out-of-scope request goal: the goals themselves trust: a trust-boundary question a gate cannot settle infra: an infrastructure change owner review: owner/repo#n at <sha7> a change under your owner_paths exception: owner/repo#n at <sha7>: <gap> accepting one safety gap (tests, gates, CI, threads) at one head plan: approving the plan view at the end of a plan pass breaking: owner/repo#n at <sha7>: <what breaks>. Announced at <link>. Proceed? shipping a breaking change (a major), after its announcement

Any other question is sent back to the model: decide it, record the assumption, go on. The model never asks whether to continue planned work. Each question comes once, with a recommendation.

Your answers outlive compaction and new sessions. Every session start lists the answers of the last 7 days, and a question you answered in that window (same class and text, case and spacing aside) is sent back with your answer and its date. A question on a new head or PR differs in its text, so it reaches you; a plan: question reaches you again once the plan has an item you have not approved.

Why: your attention is the scarcest resource on the team. The report counts your prompts and how often you chose the recommendation; a kind of question you always answer the same way becomes a rule at the next retro.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
Sometimes a safety gap is acceptable: a hotfix without the security gate at 2am. (A process gap, such as a spec rule misfiring on an old feature at standard tier, never reaches you: it does not block, and the merge records it for the retro.) You accept it with an exception: question. WUWEI records the ruling, drops that gap at that head, and adds a follow-up item to the plan that closes it later. The report lists open exceptions.

The gap in the question must be the gap as wuwei evidence prints it. Case, spacing, end marks and a printed [waiting] do not matter. For a gate gap, the gates it names also work: security for gates missing at head <sha7>: security. A part of a gap waives nothing: security does not drop gates missing at head <sha7>: quality, security, and e drops no gap at all. A gap that ends in an analysis.md finding row runs to the row's last |, so a sentence inside the row stays in the gap. Each open finding row and each checklist with an unchecked box is its own gap, so accepting one leaves the others holding the merge.

Why: an accepted gap is a debt. Exceptions expire into work, never into silence.

docs.title: ADRs
docs.text:
When you answer a one-way: question, the planner records the decision as a short Architecture Decision Record (context, decision, consequences) through the item's PR. It goes where the repository keeps its ADRs: an existing docs/adr/ or docs/decisions/, else the item's spec folder. When your answer re-confirms an existing ADR, the planner amends that ADR instead of adding a file.

Why: the reason for a hard decision outlives the session that took it, and the next person (or agent) who wants to reverse it should find it.

docs.title: The doors
docs.text:
The doors are WUWEI's police powers: a short, closed list of refusals for what cannot be taken back. Everything else passes and is recorded. Adding a door is a design change, not a fix.

Door Refused Why Merge with gaps a merge by any route (gh pr merge, a REST PUT on .../pulls/<n>/merge or .../ccr/auto_merge in any spelling, a GitHub MCP merge tool) while the PR has safety gaps (a breaking change without its announcement and your confirmation among them), listing them; arming auto-merge passes when only CI is still running (a required check not yet created included) or only GitHub's own merge hold is left the moment code reaches everyone is the moment evidence matters Ungated PR a PR opened ready for review (gh pr create, gh pr new, a REST POST on repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls or a GitHub MCP create tool without draft), the flip to ready (gh pr ready, a REST POST on .../pulls/<n>/ccr/ready_for_review, MCP update_pull_request with draft false) or a reviewer request on a draft (gh pr edit --add-reviewer, .../requested_reviewers, MCP reviewers or request_copilot_review) before the gates the diff needs pass at the head, listing them, or the flip and the reviewer request on a draft until CI is green at the head (a check failing, running or not started, or a required check not run), naming it; a draft opens before them, and an owner exception for the gap at that PR and head opens the flip and the reviewer request the gates read the draft while CI runs, and review and merge start at a gated head with green CI, so no gate races a merge Admin bypass gh pr merge --admin (or --admin=true, --admin=1), a gh api write to repositories/<id>/... (spell it repos/<owner>/<repo>/...), a gh api graphql query WUWEI cannot read (stdin, a missing file, a file outside one plain gh call), gh api writes to protection, rulesets, statuses, collaborators, hooks, keys, secrets, environments; gh repo delete or a REST DELETE on the repository; a gh api graphql mutation that merges, arms auto-merge, opens a PR, marks one ready, requests reviewers, moves a ref, commits to a branch or changes protection or rulesets the repository's own rules are not changed from an agent session History force pushes in every form; pushes to or deletion of the default branch (a destination as git 2.43 reads it: main, heads/main or refs/heads/main after the last colon, or the ref git itself resolves a source alone to; the matching refspec :, --all, --branches and a glob whose destination can match it; a word an option takes is no refspec, and every word after the first -- or --end-of-options is one; a push of a ref named --, which git reads per worktree, and a push whose refs git cannot read in 5 s too), including the GitHub MCP push_files, create_or_update_file and delete_file tools on it or with no branch (a force push, push or delete to a git directory in a scratch folder passes in one plain git call); a git command naming push after an option before the subcommand that git 2.43 does not take, or after a -c or --config-env setting remote.*, branch.*, url.* or push.default; any git command after a -c or --config-env setting an alias or an include; gh api writes to merges, git/refs/ or contents/ on any branch published history does not come back Secrets a secret pattern or the workspace canary in an MCP call or a network command a leaked secret cannot be unleaked The record writes to the ledger (.wuwei/ledger, .wuwei/ledger.jsonl, or .wuwei itself) in the spellings sh expands (//, /./, .., globs such as .wuwei/* and .w*/ledger, braces such as {l,}edger); writes to the cache (.wuwei/cache), whose entries feed gate inputs (removing a cache file passes); find with -delete, -exec, -execdir, -fprint, -fprintf or -fls on those paths (the cache included); a path in a python -c body; a writer or a redirect after cd .wuwei, or in a command whose -C, --chdir or -D value names .wuwei (env -C .wuwei, sudo -D .wuwei); git clean with -x, -X or an exclude that is not a plain word, unless every pathspec and -C dir is a plain word lying outside .wuwei (dry runs included), and git clean after any git option but -C or with GIT_ in the command; writes under the harness's transcripts (.claude/projects) in the same spellings, reads passing, and Claude Code's memory (a file directly in <project>/memory, by Write, Edit, a redirect, tee, sed -i, truncate or rm on its literal path) writable; a hand-made wuwei hook call, or a literal -m wuwei hook through any interpreter an audit you can edit is not an audit Your attention an owner question (AskUserQuestion, or request_user_input in Codex) without an owner class a question the process answers costs you for nothing Infrastructure asked, not refused: terraform, tofu, pulumi, kubectl and helm writes go to the harness's own prompt a one-way door you decide

A door that cannot read its evidence stays shut. Every other hook fails open: if a hook breaks, the work goes on and hook.error is recorded. The one exception: if the PreToolUse hook fails before it can judge (an import, its arguments, the version read), every PreToolUse call is refused. An account with no password-database entry is not such a failure: the doors still judge, and owner answers and seat stops are recorded as unconfirmed.

docs.title: How strongly a door holds
docs.text:
A hook on your machine is cooperative: it stops honest mistakes and visible workarounds, but anything running as your user can write any local file. WUWEI is explicit about that with three levels, which wuwei doctor prints per repository:

Level Meaning Example wall the code host or the credentials make it impossible a ruleset that requires PRs and blocks force pushes refused a hook refuses it with the reason the merge door on a repo without a ruleset detected it can happen, and the audit shows it a merge done in the browser shows as an exception in the report

To turn refusals into walls: give the agents their own GitHub identity (an App or machine user with write access and no admin), protect default branches with rulesets, require code-owner review on your owner_paths, and keep infrastructure and publishing credentials out of the agents' environment.

docs.title: Andon
docs.text:
From the Toyota production line: anyone who sees a problem that breaks the line pulls the cord. A seat that finds a repository broken for everyone (its base branch red, a leaked secret, a broken shared dependency) runs wuwei andon owner/repo --reason "...". New builds in that repository wait until the cord is cleared with --clear; other repositories keep flowing.

Why: building on a broken base multiplies the damage. Stopping one stream, by the agents' own judgment, is responsible autonomy; stopping everything is not.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
A pull request is done when its safety evidence is complete. wuwei evidence owner/repo#n lists one PR's safety gaps; wuwei status lists every open item's. Each gap is actionable (the team can close it now), waiting (CI running, CI not started at a code head with no checks yet, the code host unreadable, an andon) or yours (an owner review).

WUWEI never asks how the work was done. A test is in the diff or it is not; a reviewer passed this head or did not.

Evidence Applies Kind Why The WUWEI footer naming the item every PR process work outside the plan is visible, and the audit can trace each change to a goal The repository's PR template sections when the repo has a template process the repository's own process comes first A test in the diff, or No test: <reason> code changes safety test first is the cheapest defect filter there is Under about 400 changed lines, or Size: <reason> every PR, generated files aside process small batches fail less and are reviewed better Rollback: <how to undo> full tier, or owner_paths touched process a change you cannot undo deserves a plan for undoing it The spec engine's steps, judged by their artifacts at the head standard and full, when the repo has .specify/ or openspec/ process at standard, safety at full the agreement about what to build is part of the change A breaking change: an Announcement: link, then the owner's confirmation at the head a declared break, or one the arch gate finds safety clients you break should hear it from you first, and you decide whether it ships The gates the diff needs, passed before the PR turned ready the diff, under the tier's ceiling safety independent review before anyone else reads the code, and only the reviews the change calls for CI green every PR safety the repository's own checks Every check the base branch requires ran (see required checks) a base branch with protection or rulesets that require checks safety a check that never ran is not a pass, and an admin can merge past GitHub's own hold A review status settled (see review statuses) a commit status from a workflow the repo runs on pull_request_review safety a gate waiting on a reviewer needs someone to act; it is not a build Every review thread answered every PR safety people's questions are obligations A reviewer requested every PR process a PR nobody is asked to read is not reviewed Owner review: your approving review, or your owner review: answer, at the head (a breaking: or exception: answer is not one) owner_paths touched safety what you chose to review yourself Not stale (under three days open) every PR process inventory rots; flow over stock

docs.title: Review statuses
docs.text:
Some repositories publish their approval rule as a commit status, from a workflow that runs on pull_request_review (ai-stacks' Review Gate). WUWEI follows the status's target_url to its workflow run and compares the run's workflow with the workflows the repository has run on pull_request_review (its last 100 such runs, read once a day, and only when a head has an unsettled status). A match is review evidence, not CI:

Status Gap pending waiting on review: <context> failure change request outstanding: <context>

Both are actionable safety gaps: someone has to ask for a review or answer the change request, and the merge stays refused until then, with or without auto-merge. When the Actions host cannot be read, the status stays CI (CI running or CI failing), never a pass.

Why: a review gate read as CI tells the team to wait for a build that already finished, or to fix a build that is not red.

docs.title: Required checks
docs.text:
WUWEI reads the checks the PR's base branch requires: from branch protection (through the branch read, which needs only read access) and from the rulesets that apply to the branch. It keeps the answer 15 minutes per repository and branch.

What WUWEI finds Gap Arming auto-merge CI settled, and a required check has no check run and no status of that name on the head required check not run at <sha7>: <names> held CI still running, and a required check has no run yet required check not run yet at <sha7>: <names> (waiting) passes the protection or rulesets read fails or is malformed required checks unreadable on <branch>: <error> (waiting) held GitHub reports the PR's mergeable_state blocked, and WUWEI has no other safety gap for it GitHub reports the merge blocked for a reason WUWEI cannot name: read the merge box on the PR (waiting) passes

Every one of these gaps holds a direct merge. GitHub creates a job's check run only once the job is queued, so while CI runs a missing check may simply not exist yet. GitHub's auto-merge waits on its own required checks and its own hold, so arming it then is safe. A required check that ran and failed or is still running reads as CI failing or CI running. A failed read is read again next time.

Release PRs. release-please pushes with the workflow token, and a push with that token starts no workflow. Its PR then carries required checks not run, with a pointer to this remedy. The way through:

  1. Set a repository secret the release workflow passes to release-please as its token. In this repository that is RELEASE_PAT, which .github/workflows/release.yml already reads before the workflow token. Use a fine-grained token or a GitHub App token with contents and pull-requests write. Its pushes start the Tests workflow on the release PR.
  2. Until then, close and reopen the release PR. A reopen by a person starts the pull_request workflows at its head.
  3. Or record an owner exception: at that head.

A release PR sometimes does get its checks (when a person's push or reopen started them), so one release PR with green checks does not show the secret is set.

Why: release-please pushed with the workflow token, so release PRs #1156 and #1157 had none of main's required checks on their heads. GitHub reported them blocked, but an admin could merge past that, and WUWEI read only the checks that reported.

docs.title: The spec engine
docs.text:
When a repository uses a spec engine, its steps are part of the evidence at standard and full. WUWEI does not watch the steps run; it reads their artifacts at the PR head, in every feature directory the diff touches, so a later commit that only updates tasks.md still counts.

Engine standard full adds spec-kit (.specify/, features in specs/<feature>/) spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md with every task checked (implement done) a ## Clarifications section in spec.md (clarify ran), analysis.md with no open CRITICAL or HIGH row (analyze ran clean), every item in checklists/ checked OpenSpec (openspec/, changes in openspec/changes/<change>/) proposal.md, at least one capability spec under specs/, tasks.md with every task checked

Each open CRITICAL or HIGH row is its own gap, and so is each checklist with an unchecked box. A row longer than 100 characters is cut at its last cell edge within them, unless another open row would print the same text; then both print whole. An owner who accepts one has seen the gap that the exception waives.

Why: a spec nobody finished is worse than no spec, because it looks like agreement. Checking the artifacts, not the commands, keeps the rule true whichever way the steps were run.

At standard the steps are process fit: a misfit is recorded, never blocking. At full they are safety gaps and hold the merge, because full is the tier for work where building the wrong thing is expensive.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text:
A breaking change is a major version under SemVer 2.0.0: an incompatible change to the public API a project declares. Its clients cannot be un-broken, so it is close to a one-way door. In a repository WUWEI audits, the arch gate reads that repository's declared public API, or what it documents for clients when it declares none.

WUWEI's own public API is:

  • the CLI commands, flags, exit codes and the output documented for scripts;
  • the config keys and their defaults;
  • the ledger, state and verdict file formats;
  • the PR body lines and owner question shapes that seats and owners write;
  • the hook input and output contract;
  • the skill names (/wuwei-run, /wuwei-watch, /wuwei-close, /wuwei-rules, and the old name of a renamed skill while its alias ships), the plugin name and the marketplace name;
  • the agent role names, which the config's models rows name;
  • the owner-written files: .wuwei/goals.md, .wuwei/standards.md and the plan file format.

The gate reads this list, or a project's own declaration, at the base commit, never from the PR's own head, so a PR cannot shrink the API it is judged by. A change is classified by what it does to that API:

Bump The change major a documented element is removed, renamed or given a different meaning or shape; an input every client must now give; a documented exit code changes meaning minor a new capability that existing clients need not use; a new check that is off by default or only adds information patch a fix of behaviour that contradicted the documented public API at the base, including a closed guard bypass and a gap the docs already promised; docs; internals

A fix makes the code do what the docs already said, so it is a patch even when WUWEI now refuses or reports more. Refusing or reporting more is a patch only under that condition: the old behaviour contradicted the documented public API. A new rule that asks every PR for something the docs never asked is an input every client must now give, so a major. An exit code is judged by its meaning, not by which inputs reach it: when wuwei evidence exits 1 on one more PR because a documented rule is now checked strictly, 1 still means gaps, so that is a patch. A change with any major part is a major. When the gate is unsure which bump applies, it escalates to you with Breaking: yes.

Versions 2.0.0 to 4.0.0 were bumped under the earlier rule, where any visible change in behaviour counted as breaking, and from 4.1.0 the SemVer policy applies.

WUWEI finds a breaking change three ways: the PR declares it (a ! in the title, a BREAKING CHANGE: line), the architecture gate states it (every arch verdict carries Breaking: no or Breaking: yes: <what breaks for which clients>, and yes means a major), and a change to a contract file (OpenAPI, protobuf, GraphQL, JSON schema) takes the arch gate at any tier so it looks. A patch is a fix: commit and a minor a feat:, as release-please bumps them; only a major takes a !.

Before a major merges it needs evidence, in order:

  1. An Announcement: <url> line: one http(s) URL alone on the line, without brackets. It points at a client communication that already exists: a PR or issue comment, or a published release note or migration guide. A changelog entry written at release does not count.
  2. Your confirmation, asked once the announcement exists: breaking: owner/repo#n at <sha7>: <what breaks>. Announced at <link>. Proceed?. It binds to that head; a change after it asks again.

Why: a break nobody announced is an outage for someone else. The team does the work of finding and announcing it; you decide whether it ships. A major that is not one costs clients an upgrade review for nothing, so a fix of a documented rule ships as a patch, with release notes.

docs.title: Gates before the PR, chosen by the diff
docs.text:
The gates run before review: the PR opens as a draft, the gates read its head while CI runs, and gh pr ready and reviewer requests are refused until the gates pass at its head, so reviewers and the merge only ever see gated code. They also wait for green CI at the head, naming what holds it (a review-triggered status is review evidence, not CI); a red check found after the gates pass goes back to the builder, and its fix is a new head.

The tier is a ceiling and the diff decides what runs under it:

The diff Gates prose only, at any size (.md, .rst and .adoc files outside the spec folders, other than the files seats load such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, charters, agents and skills; LICENSE; NOTICE), or specs of 200 lines or fewer with no contract none code quality risky paths (auth, sessions, tokens, secrets, crypto, SQL, migrations, policies, infrastructure, CI, dependency manifests) or owner_paths, at standard + security a contract file or a spec contract (a file under a spec's contracts/ folder) at any tier, or at standard more than 200 changed lines that are not prose (code, specs, .txt files, code under docs/, the files seats load) or 10 code files + arch full tier all four

docs.title: The smart tier
docs.text:
smart is the default for new items. The lead classifies each item with Cynefin and records the domain with one line of evidence (--domain "clear: <why>"); the gates start from the standard rows above and the domain and the measured signals at the head only add to them:

Domain or signal Gates clear the standard rows above complicated, on a trust path (auth, sessions, tokens, secrets, permissions, grants, policies) + arch complex, or no domain recorded, or a domain in another spelling quality, security and arch, a short How this fails and the spec engine's artifacts, which hold the merge a changed Python function whose decision nodes (if, loop, except, assert, boolean operator, comprehension, match case, conditional expression), read with ast at the base and the head and summed over functions of one name, rise to 10 or more (McCabe complexity over 10); a head that cannot be read or parsed counts as a rise + security a code patch that names what a guard waives or refuses (deny, ask, allow, refuse, waive, excepted, exception, permissionDecision, PROCESS, DUTY), or a code file with no patch + arch the promise marked in doubt (--in-doubt) + goal

A model-written or seat-written field can only raise the set: a clear domain on an owner path still takes security, and on a guard change still takes arch.

A one-line config flag costs one gate. After a fix round only the gate that found the problem re-reads. After review comments, a delta of docs, or of at most 20 lines off risky paths, carries the earlier passes; a larger one is re-read by the one gate it needs (security for risky paths, arch for a contract, quality otherwise). The delta is what moved in the PR's own diff against its base, not everything between the two heads. A merge of the base that leaves the PR's own patches alone (line numbers aside) carries the passes, as does a change only to files the workspace declares generated with a dated line in .wuwei/standards.md, such as - Generated (acme/app, 2026-10-22): guide/* src/version.py. The line applies off risky, owner and contract paths: a file there still counts, whatever the line names. When the error budget is overrun (smart rises to standard), or a light item touches a trust path (auth, sessions, tokens, secrets, permissions, grants, policies) outside docs, the raised tier takes its full gate set.

Why: gates that run after the PR opens race the merge, and four gates on a one-line change cost more than they find. Review cost follows risk.

docs.title: Attested verdicts
docs.text:
A verdict counts only when WUWEI attested it. When a sentinel stops, the SubagentStop hook reads the file it names (Verdict file: <path>), checks its shape, and records its hash, gate, item, head, confidence and the agent that wrote it. A malformed verdict goes back to the reviewer once with the format. A file edited after attestation no longer counts, except that a finding (FIX or ESCALATE) still holds as recorded: replacing it cannot turn it into a pass. A verdict counts only at an ancestor of the PR head. A pass counts only for this PR, for its repository alone, or when no PR is named (an imported 0.34 verdict); a finding holds from any PR of the item. A later pass at an older head never clears a finding. At the same head it clears a FIX only when it names that file on a Supersedes: <item>/<file> line, for a finding closed outside the diff; an ESCALATE stays the owner's. Otherwise only a pass at a newer head on the PR's line clears it. Supersedes: clears gates only: an arch Breaking: no clears a Breaking: yes only from a newer head on the PR's line, for this PR or its repository alone. The create and ready doors read no PR yet, so there a pass for any PR of the item in that repository counts. A gate whose only pass named another PR reads missing: re-run it with PR: <owner/repo>#<n>. A seat that writes over another seat's verdict is sent back to write its own file beside it. When the stop cannot read the seat's last message, the handback to the lead carries it, and the verdict is attested from there. A verdict file that does not count is never silent: the board names it and why (its shape, or that no sentinel attested it). An attested pass that does not count for this PR or head shows only as the gate missing.

Why: a review is evidence only if a reviewer wrote it and it has not changed since. The hook checks the file at stop, however it was written, so a shell edit cannot slip past the lint.

docs.title: Duties
docs.text: A duty is work the team owes that does not hold the merge but reaches the team until it is done: asking for review where the team asks (see review requests), and, when a check is red, re-requesting an approval given at an older commit (the approval is named with its commit, so nobody re-runs a review gate that wants an approval at the head). One team row, first on the board, names the seats nobody runs: orchestration: open PRs with no shepherd seat running when more than two PRs are open, and orchestration: gates owed with no gate seat running when a gate is missing at a head with no failing check: gates start at push, while CI runs or before it starts, and a red head goes to its builder first. A seat runs when this session started it today and no stop or unconfirmed row followed; a Codex job writes no seat row and never counts. The lines carry no count, so a Stop reminds once while the state holds. Duties show on the board and in the Stop reminder, like safety gaps.

docs.title: Safety and process
docs.text:
Only safety gaps hold a merge and reach the team while it works: a test, the gates at the head, green CI, answered threads, owner review, a breaking change's announcement and confirmation, the spec engine's steps at full, and evidence that can be read. Everything else is process fit: the plan link, the PR template, small batches, the Rollback: line, the spec engine's steps below full, a requested reviewer, staleness. Process fit never blocks and is never shown on the board or asked about; the merge records it, the report lists it, and the steward turns a rule that keeps misfiring, or keeps being skipped, into a fix.

Why: continuous flow. Neither you nor the model should be distracted by a rule that does not fit this change. The audit still sees every misfit, and the process learns from them.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text: For a safety gap only, you can accept one gap at one head as an exception (see decisions). The gap disappears from that head's evidence, the exception stays on the record, and a follow-up item in the plan closes it later. Only the gap the exception names exactly disappears; a part of a gap waives nothing. When it is a gate gap, the verdict ... not counted lines under it go too, and the ready door lets that draft turn ready or ask reviewers at that head.

docs.title: When evidence cannot be read
docs.text: An unreadable code host is a waiting gap, never a pass. A merge whose evidence cannot be read stays refused.

docs.title: Hooks: the sensei
docs.text:
A good teacher shows the form before the move, watches without commenting on every step, corrects on the spot, and is strict where it matters. WUWEI's hooks play that role.

Stage When What happens Teach before a move the session starts with the way of working, the Decisions and Done rules, where the planner charter, goals and standards are, and the board; before gh pr create, the PR standard with a ready body Watch during every tool call is traced, silently Correct right after a new PR is told what it still lacks; a one-way answer is turned into an ADR note Stop where it matters the doors; a malformed verdict sent back; one reminder when the team tries to stop with work it can close Stay quiet when all is well no notes, no reminders, a short report

docs.title: The hooks
docs.text:
Hook Role SessionStart orientation within Claude Code's 10,000-character cap on hook context: the CLI path, the way of working, _common.md Decisions and Done, the paths of the planner charter, goals and .wuwei/standards.md, your answers of the last 7 days (those not recorded first, with their reason), the board with how many items it left out; at every start, compaction included PreToolUse the doors; the PR standard once per session before gh pr create; owner questions without a class sent back, and a question you answered in the last 7 days sent back with your answer; a seat launch for an item another live session holds sent back, naming that session PostToolUse a trace per call; what a new PR lacks; owner answers kept as answer.pending, then recorded as prompts, rulings, exceptions once the session transcript shows them (on the planner's next call, before its doors, since Claude Code writes the answer after the hook) SubagentStop every seat's stop recorded with its tokens and confidence; a sentinel's verdict linted and attested; only when the session transcript shows the seat's launch Stop a reminder only when actionable work is new since the last one, naming only what changed; once to arm the watch or to plan when the flow would stall; never a loop

Why the transcript: a hand-made hook call could otherwise write a ruling or a seat stop the owner never gave. An answer or stop the transcript does not show is recorded as answer.unconfirmed or seat.unconfirmed with the check that failed: at once, or for an answer once its tool_result row holds a different answer to that question or no toolUseResult answers (its text never counts), or after 10 minutes with no row. Each question in a batch counts on its own, and an answer that is not recorded never blocks the planner's Stop: its note comes on the next tool call. A session that ends before it confirms an answer leaves the answer's answer.pending row, which reads as unconfirmed. An error while the next call confirms an answer is a hook.error; the doors still judge that call.

Seat reports outside auto mode: Claude Code refuses SubagentHandback there, so SubagentStop keeps each seat's last message under .wuwei/reports/. The planner's next tool call or Stop gives a kept report once. When a task notification in the session transcript already holds that seat's result, the hook gives a one-line pointer to the kept file instead of the text: a queued notification can still be dropped (the kill-agents chord, an interrupt), so the planner always has a way to the report.

In a cloud session, SessionStart also pulls the wuwei/state branch and Stop pushes what changed; see cloud sessions.

docs.title: Why hooks and not only skills
docs.text:
A skill works when the model chooses to load it, and that choice is where guidance fails: the model is busy and the skill stays unread. A hook fires on the event whatever the model chose. So the standards live once (in charters and skills), and hooks deliver them at the moment they apply.

Hooks see tool calls and lifecycle events, not intent. Guidance needed before the first tool call stays in the charters and the session start.

docs.title: The Stop reminder
docs.text:
When the session tries to end its turn while there is work it can close now (a PR without a test, an item without a PR), the Stop hook blocks once with the list, at most ten lines, and says how many waiting items it left out. It never loops and never nags: while a seat this session started is still running it stays silent (the seat's completion wakes the planner anyway; a seat a dead session left without a stop does not count), the same set of gaps does not block twice, waits (CI, the owner, plan approval, an andon) never count, a closed day is quiet, and a turn already continued by a Stop hook always passes.

Two more reminders keep the flow from stalling on the owner's nudge, each once per session: when only waiting work is left and no watch pass ran in the last hour, it says nothing will wake the session for the waiting work unless a check-in or PR subscription is armed, which WUWEI cannot see, and asks it to arm /wuwei-watch on a schedule; when the queue is empty and goals are set, it asks for a plan pass from the goals.

Several sessions can share one workspace. The board counts the live seats of every session (a seat.started row with no stop or unconfirmed row, at most six hours old) and names the session holding each item, so the WIP limit, the seat ceiling and the team row see them all. A launch whose brief names an item another live session holds is sent back. The brief's item is its first line that starts with Item:, else its first Item:.

Why: it turns "honour the promise" into a habit without turning it into a trap.

docs.title: Learning
docs.text:
At each checkpoint the steward reads the report, the ledger and the verdicts and writes the retro to .wuwei/retro/<date>.md, with at most three proposals. Process rules land in .wuwei/standards.md, which the session reads at start and every seat receives in its brief. Changes to a repository (its memory or skills) become plan items, built and reviewed like any change.

Why: a process that does not learn repeats its mistakes, and a process that only grows collapses under its own rules. Both directions are needed.

docs.title: Defect vaccines
docs.text:
Every escaped defect (a revert, or a follow-up fix to the same lines) is traced to the merge it came from and the gates that passed it, with their stated confidence. The steward proposes a regression test item and one line under the gate that should have caught it: quality: an error path that ends a long job on a rate-limit error. The planner passes those lines to every brief, and the gates check them first.

Why: the cheapest defect to catch is one you have already seen escape.

docs.title: Calibration and yield
docs.text:
Builders and gates state their confidence (low, medium, high) on every handoff and verdict. The report shows each gate's yield (verdicts and how many found something to fix) and the confidence of the verdicts that passed an escaped change.

Why: knowing when you do not know is the core of responsible autonomy. An overconfident gate gets stricter standards; a gate that never finds anything is a cost to question.

docs.title: Error budget
docs.text:
From site reliability engineering: when a repository's change failure rate over 28 days (reverts and failed production deployments over merges, with at least five merges) goes over 15 percent, every tier in that repository rises one step until it recovers. Light changes get the full gate set; standard changes get the goal gate.

Why: autonomy should be earned by results and lost by escapes, automatically, without anyone configuring it.

docs.title: Skills and memory
docs.text:
When seats keep re-learning a repository fact (how to run its tests, a convention, a trap), the steward proposes a line for that repository's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. When the same multi-step procedure recurs three or more times (a hotfix release, a migration), it proposes a project skill under .claude/skills/. Both land through a PR in that repository. AGENTS.md is read by other harnesses too, so the memory travels. WUWEI never writes your personal memory.

Why: an agent that relearns the same fact every session pays for it every session.

docs.title: Empty the cup
docs.text:
A rule in .wuwei/standards.md that caught nothing in 30 days is proposed for removal. A new rule starts as a note for its first five days, so its false alarms show before it costs anyone time.

Why: rules that never fire still cost attention. A process stays light only if it forgets.

docs.title: Questions that become rules
docs.text: The report counts your prompts and how often you chose the recommendation. A kind of question you keep answering the same way becomes a proposal that the process decides it.

docs.title: The weekly sample
docs.text: Each week the report picks one merged PR at random as a sample for you. It is not a question: read its evidence comment if you want to. It is how you audit the auditor.

docs.title: Many repositories
docs.text: WUWEI is built for one person's team working across several repositories, and for adopters who want the same process everywhere without forcing every repository into one shape.

docs.title: One workspace, many repositories
docs.text: A workspace (.wuwei/) lists its repositories in repos. There is one plan, one board, one ledger, one report and one set of standards across all of them. Each plan item names its repository.

docs.title: The same principles everywhere
docs.text:
What does not vary by repository is the backbone:

  • the evidence contract and the tiers;
  • the doors;
  • the owner question classes and the reversibility and confidence rule;
  • the charters and the standards;
  • the learning loop.

These live in the plugin and in .wuwei/standards.md, not in per-repository configuration. There is nothing to configure differently, so nothing drifts.

docs.title: The shape of each repository
docs.text:
What adapts is read, not configured:

Fact Read from PR template sections the repository's template Spec engine .specify/ or openspec/ Default branch the code host Protection and rulesets the code host (and wuwei doctor shows the door strength) CI the repository's own checks Change failure rate its merges, reverts and production deployments Repository memory its CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md

Why: a process that ignores a repository's own conventions fights its maintainers. Reading them means WUWEI fills gaps instead of adding a second process.

docs.title: Consistency you can see
docs.text:
• wuwei doctor prints, per repository, how strongly each door holds (wall, refused or detected). A repository you cannot protect with rulesets is visible as one.
  • The report shows each repository's change failure rate and whether its tiers are raised.
  • Unplanned PRs are listed per repository.

docs.title: For a team
docs.text: Each person runs their own workspace. To share the backbone across a team, keep the standards you agree on in a repository the team owns and copy them into each workspace's .wuwei/standards.md; the retro of each workspace proposes changes back as a PR to that repository. Repository memory (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, project skills) already lives in each repository and is shared through the normal review.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
wuwei report (and each checkpoint) shows the day from the records, never from memory:

  • plan passes, checkpoints, items done and parked, and what changed since the last checkpoint;
  • the board;
  • every merge, and whether it went through WUWEI's check or was an exception;
  • the doors: refusals and their reasons, questions sent back to the model, infrastructure asks, notes and Stop reminders;
  • your prompts;
  • seats and verdicts;
  • learning: escaped defects traced to their gates, each repository's change failure rate and whether its tiers are raised, unplanned PRs, gate yield, tokens by role, open exceptions, the weekly sample;
  • telemetry: tool calls, outward calls, hook errors;
  • the ledger's integrity.

Why: you should never have to ask where things stand, and nothing the team did should be invisible.

docs.title: DORA
docs.text:
wuwei report --dora gives the four keys per repository from the code host alone: lead time (PR open to merge), deployment frequency (deployments, or releases when a repository never deploys), change failure rate (change failures over merges, at most 1) and time to restore. A change failure is a revert (a merged PR whose title starts with the word revert) or a run of failed production deployments until the next green deployment of the same environment. Production means an environment GitHub flags as production, or one named with prod or production as a word (not preprod, pre-prod or non-prod); only the newest 100 production deployments in the window are read. Time to restore is the median time from the first failed deployment of a run to that green one, unmeasured when nothing was restored.

Why: reading the code host means the history is complete from day one, even for work done before WUWEI or without it.

docs.title: Telemetry
docs.text: Every tool call is a line in .wuwei/traces.jsonl (session, agent, tool, a short target with secrets redacted, duration). It stays on your machine. telemetry = false turns it off.

docs.title: The ledger
docs.text:
.wuwei/ledger/ records what cannot be read from git or the code host: plan changes, attestations, rulings, exceptions, refusals, andon, checkpoints. Each clone writes its own file, <clone>.jsonl, so sessions syncing through git never edit the same rows; a 0.34-era ledger.jsonl is still read. Each row carries the hash of the row before it in its file and a format version. wuwei verify checks every chain; a broken link names its file and line.

Why: an audit trail is only worth something if editing it shows.

docs.title: Replay cases
docs.text:
wuwei evidence owner/repo#n --record <dir> saves a real PR's code-host answers, a copy of the workspace, the clock and the gaps WUWEI found. Copy the directory under tests/replay/ and every future version of WUWEI must give the same answer for it.

Why: the auditor is held to its own past answers. A change that would have passed a PR it once refused shows up as a failing test, not as a surprise.

docs.title: Models and effort
docs.text:
Each seat runs on the model and effort its work needs. The planner charter holds one table for every repository running WUWEI (charters/planner.md, "Model and effort"). The planner follows it, departs from it with a recorded reason, and is never refused. WUWEI advises; you decide.

Why: a seat on too weak a model costs fix rounds and escaped defects; a seat on too strong a setting costs tokens for nothing. One written table makes the choice the same each time, and the retro can measure it.

docs.title: The inputs
docs.text:
The table reads only signals WUWEI already computes for every item:

  • the item's tier (light, standard, full), after the change failure rate rule raises it a step;
  • risky, owner or contract paths: the risky paths, the owner paths and the contract files the diff touches (a wider set than the trust paths that raise a light item to standard);
  • the item's history: failed fix rounds, gate blockers the builder missed, a park for a design problem, a one-way decision.

docs.title: Why each row
docs.text:
Seat Setting Why lead Opus 5.5 xhigh ranking and red-teaming the plan is long-horizon reasoning, and a wrong plan wastes every seat after it builder Sonnet 5.5 medium at light, Opus 5.5 medium at standard, Opus 5.5 high at full or on risky, owner or contract paths Sonnet 5.5 is Anthropic's choice for everyday coding; Opus 5.5 for complex agentic coding; those paths are intelligence-sensitive sentinel-security Opus 5.5 high, xhigh at full or on risky, owner or contract paths a missed trust defect is the costliest escape sentinel-arch Opus 5.5 high coupling and contracts need reasoning across the whole design sentinel-quality Sonnet 5.5 high, Opus 5.5 high at full or on risky, owner or contract paths a second model family on routine heads; the stronger model where a missed test costs most sentinel-goal Sonnet 5.5 high reads the promise against the diff; a different model than the builder at full shepherd Sonnet 5.5 medium, Opus 5.5 high for a conflict where both sides changed logic most PR work is routine; a logic conflict is not steward Opus 5.5 high the retro weighs evidence across the day lookups and searches Haiku 5.5 low Anthropic names Haiku 5.5 for simple, speed-critical work and low effort for simple subagent tasks

Where two settings in a row apply, the later one holds. The session's own model is yours. The table never names it.

docs.title: Escalation and diversity
docs.text:
The ladder runs Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 at medium, high and xhigh, then Fable 5.1. A seat moves up one step after a failed fix round or after a gate finds a blocker the builder missed. Fable 5.1, Anthropic's most capable model, is the step for an item parked as a design problem (two failed fix rounds) and for a one-way decision. Under zero data retention Fable may be unavailable; there the top step is Opus 5.5 at max. A step never lowers effort: Sonnet 5.5 at high steps to Opus 5.5 at high.

A seat class steps down only on retro evidence: 10 merged items on the lower setting with no escaped defect. The count makes the rule testable.

At least one gate per head runs on a different model than the builder, so the reviews do not share every blind spot. When the table would put every gate on the builder's model (a light item, or a standard item on risky, owner or contract paths), the quality gate takes the other of Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, at high.

After a fix, a delta is re-read by one gate, and the passes from the earlier head carry to it. Those carried passes count toward diversity, so the gate that re-reads keeps its own model. The limit: if the gate on the other model passed the earlier head and the fix changed what it read, the delta has no fresh review from another model.

Haiku 5.5, the weakest tier, never runs a gate on risky, owner or contract paths. That floor is not a departure the planner can record with a reason: breaking it is an exception: for you.

docs.title: Effort
docs.text:
• Set effort on every call. Opus 5.5 defaults to medium, and defaults differ between models and between the API and Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5 is high on the API, medium in Claude Code).
  • Use at least high for intelligence-sensitive work, max when correctness matters more than cost, and low for simple subagent tasks.
  • Before moving a seat to a cheaper model, measure the stronger model at a lower effort. Anthropic reports that tuning effort is often a better lever than switching models.
  • Judge cost per completed item, not per request: a cheap seat that needs a second round costs more.

docs.title: How Claude Code applies it
docs.text:
• The planner passes model and effort on each Agent call, with full model IDs (claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-haiku-5-5, claude-fable-5-1). A family alias such as opus can resolve to the session's own model when it is in that family, and sonnet resolves to an older version on some providers. The per-call effort parameter needs Claude Code v2.1.292 or later.
  • On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry, model IDs are the provider's own, so claude-sonnet-5-5 may not resolve and the seat can fall back to the session's model without notice. There, set your models rows to the provider's IDs, or pass the aliases with ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL and ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL pinned.
  • The brief's first line is Model: <model> <effort> (<row>). A departure adds Model reason: <one line>.
  • Model precedence: the call's model parameter, then the agent file's model frontmatter, then CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then the session model. Four cases change that order:
  • setting CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE puts the variable first;
  • before Claude Code v2.1.251, the variable came first anyway;
  • an installed mod that sets a model in its agent.spawn hook replaces the per-call parameter;
  • a value your organization's availableModels blocks is substituted: a family alias takes the newest permitted version of that family, and a full ID runs on the session's model.
  • Effort precedence: CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL beats every other effort setting, the per-call parameter included. A workspace that sets it turns WUWEI's effort advice off. A managed maxEffortLevel, or an organization effort cap, still limits the level a seat runs at.
  • What a hook can see: the hooks page lists model in the Agent call's tool_input and not effort, though a session transcript of 2026-10-18 shows the call's input holds effort when the planner passes it. The brief's first line records the effort asked for either way. What ran is visible too: the PostToolUse response carries resolvedModel, the model the seat started on, and PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SubagentStop inputs carry effort.level, the level in effect (also $CLAUDE_EFFORT in Bash).
  • wuwei agents build writes each role's default (the row's first setting, standard for the builder) into its agent file as model: and effort:, so a launch with no model still runs on the table.
  • On each Agent launch the hook compares the role, model and effort with the table at the item's tier (from the brief's Item: line, raised one step when the cached change failure rate says so). On a departure with no Model reason: line it adds a note naming the table's setting; it never refuses or rewrites the call. It cannot see the diff's paths at launch, so a setting the row gives on risky, owner or contract paths, or for a logic conflict, counts as a fit. A Haiku gate gets the note even with a reason line or a models row.
  • Each launch records the model that ran, the model and effort asked for, the reason and the item (unrecorded or unmeasured where the hook cannot read them). A gate's verdict row copies the model and effort.
  • Your own models rows in .wuwei/config.toml override any table row, for example models = {"builder light" = "opus medium"}. A row for a role and tier wins over one for the role alone. A models row that puts Haiku 5.5 on a gate does not break the floor: only your exception: answer does.
  • wuwei doctor names CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL in a note row when they are set. A note never changes the doctor's exit code. With the first set, the hook leaves effort out of its note; with the second, the model.
  • /wuwei-watch may run on Sonnet 5.5 at medium effort through its own frontmatter. The skill offers that as an option, not a default.

docs.title: On Codex
docs.text:
The same table holds on Codex. The Codex column is the planner's reading of the Codex catalog:

Claude Codex Fable 5.1 gpt-6-astra Opus 5.5 gpt-6.1-sol Sonnet 5.5 gpt-6.1-sol at a lower effort, or gpt-6-luna for checklist seats Haiku 5.5 gpt-6-luna low

It reads the descriptions in Codex's model catalog ("frontier intelligence for the most demanding work", "latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work", "fast and affordable model for easier tasks"). It is not OpenAI guidance on seats, and it is unmeasured: no outcome on Codex has been recorded against it.

  • Effort keeps the same names. gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.1-sol add ultra above max ("maximum reasoning with automatic task delegation"), the Codex top step; gpt-6-luna stops at max. The catalog's default is low on gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.1-sol and medium on gpt-6-luna, so set effort here too.
  • A role file (.codex/agents/<role>.toml) accepts model and model_reasoning_effort, and the [agents] config sets default_subagent_model and default_subagent_reasoning_effort for spawned agents.
  • spawn_agent takes model and reasoning_effort only when the workspace turns on expose_spawn_agent_model_overrides (off by default). Its own guidance tells the model that spawned agents inherit the current model and not to set model unless the user asks.
  • The role files wuwei init --codex writes still name no model; writing the table into them is later work. A Codex launch is recorded with its model and effort unmeasured, and gets no note.

docs.title: Learning from it
docs.text: At each close the steward reads outcomes by seat, model and effort. The report's Learning section gives one line for each: launches, fix rounds per item, blocking findings, escapes traced to a passing gate and tokens, and how many launches had no readable model or effort. Where the numbers back it, the retro proposes a change to a row, with those numbers, as advice. See the learning loop.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text:
The model ids and effort values above are the ones these pages name.

  • Choosing the right model, Anthropic, read 2026-10-18: the selection matrix (Fable 5.1 for the highest capability, Opus 5.5 for complex agentic coding, Sonnet 5.5 for everyday coding and agent work, Haiku 5.5 for the lowest latency and sub-agent tasks), and effort as often a better lever than switching models.
  • Models overview, Anthropic, read 2026-10-18: start with Opus 5.5 for most workloads, Fable 5.1 for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work, and the API model ids.
  • Effort, Anthropic, read 2026-10-18: Opus 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium, set effort explicitly, low for simple subagent tasks, Sonnet 5.5 starts at medium for agentic coding.
  • Optimizing for cost and intelligence, Anthropic, read 2026-10-18: compare models on cost per completed task, and sweep effort on the current model, then price the stronger model at low effort, before adding a second model.
  • Subagents, Claude Code, read 2026-10-18: the model order and the cases that change it (CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE, v2.1.251, a mod's agent.spawn, availableModels), the effort frontmatter field and per-call parameter, and family alias resolution.
  • Model configuration, Claude Code, read 2026-10-18: aliases and the ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL pins, provider-specific model IDs, the effort resolution order with CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL first, maxEffortLevel, and the effort levels each model supports.
  • Hooks, Claude Code, read 2026-10-18: the Agent tool input fields (model, no effort), resolvedModel in the PostToolUse response, the common effort.level input field and $CLAUDE_EFFORT, and the 10,000-character cap on hook context.
  • Skills, Claude Code, read 2026-10-18: a skill's model and effort frontmatter, which hold for the rest of the turn.
  • Plugin components, Claude Code, read 2026-10-18: a plugin agent's frontmatter supports model and effort.
  • Codex model catalog, OpenAI Codex source at commit 8c07694, read 2026-10-18: the model descriptions, effort levels and defaults. Codex's source stands in for OpenAI documentation here.
  • Codex agent roles, OpenAI Codex source at commit 8c07694, read 2026-10-18: a role file's model and model_reasoning_effort overrides.
  • Codex spawned agent config and spawn_agent tool text, OpenAI Codex source at commit 8c07694, read 2026-10-18: the [agents] defaults, the per-call overrides and their exposure flag, and the inherit-by-default guidance.
  • Zero data retention, Claude Code, read 2026-10-18: Fable 5.1 requires data retention by default, so a zero data retention organization may not reach it.

docs.title: Harness permissions
docs.text:
Who may call which tool is decided in one place: Claude Code's own permission rules in .claude/settings.json. WUWEI does not keep a second allow list.

wuwei init merges three sets of rules into the project settings and leaves your own untouched:

Rules Contents Why allow git, gh, reading, writing and searching files everyday work should not prompt you deny force pushes, admin merges, repository deletion, edits to the ledger the doors, held by the harness as well as the hook ask terraform, tofu, pulumi, kubectl and helm writes infrastructure is your decision

Deny rules and WUWEI's hook refusals take precedence over allow rules, so allowing broadly is safe: the doors stay held.

docs.title: Allowing a tool
docs.text: To let the team post to Slack or update Linear, allow the tool the way you always would: answer "Yes, don't ask again" on the prompt, or add mcp__slack (a whole server) or mcp__linear__save_issue (one tool) to permissions.allow. WUWEI still scans every outward call for secrets and the workspace canary, whatever the rules allow.

docs.title: Fewer prompts
docs.text:
If you still see prompts you always approve, Claude Code's /fewer-permission-prompts skill reads your transcripts and proposes allow rules for them.

Why: a permission system you maintain twice drifts, and a plugin that re-asks what the harness already allows is friction for nothing.

docs.title: Effortless action
docs.text:
